narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Evergreen Office"**

A calm, green-lit office that people open every working day. The deep evergreen sidebar is the one large field of brand colour; everything the user works on sits on white paper cards over a cool office-grey floor. The brand lives in precise details rather than big gestures: the active nav rail in sprout green, the forest-green primary button, the mint wash behind a total or a hint.

Density is moderate and work-first. Screens are built from a page header, a row of summary cards, then panels with tables or lists. Colour carries meaning before it carries mood: green means done or approved, amber means waiting, brick red means missing or rejected, teal means submitted. Components are refined and restrained: thin hairlines, nearly invisible shadows, and green used only where someone is meant to act.
keyCharacteristics: Dark evergreen sidebar, light grey page, white cards.
Flat surfaces separated by 1px hairlines; shadows only on floating layers.
One primary action per view, in forest green.
Status colour is semantic and consistent across every feature.
Inter throughout, with tight negative tracking only on headings and metrics.

rules.name: The Amber Means Waiting Rule
rules.body: Amber is only for something awaiting a decision (a submitted request, a week not yet approved). Leave tags and "On leave" use Sand (`--sand`, `--sand-bg`), holidays use Violet, Probation is neutral, and a Draft week is neutral with a dashed outline.

rules.name: The Data Is Not Status Rule
rules.body: Teal, amber and brick never encode a category. If a chart or tag needs another hue, use the data colours above.

rules.name: The Status Is Sacred Rule
rules.body: Green = approved/complete, amber = pending/waiting, brick = rejected/missing, teal = submitted, grey = draft. Never reuse these hues decoratively, and never show a status in a colour other than its own.

rules.name: The One Green Button Rule
rules.body: A view has one forest-green primary button. Other actions are secondary (white with hairline) or text buttons.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: Colours are changed in `:root` of `src/styles/globals.css`, never inline. Outside `:root` the stylesheet uses only `var(--…)`; the only literals left are the rgba scrims and shadows.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text is smaller than 11px. Use 11–13px for labels and meta, 14–15px for body and table text, 18px+ for headings and values.

rules.name: The Thai-Ready Rule
rules.body: Thai text is coming. Don't rely on uppercase or letter-spacing to carry meaning, and leave line-height room for Thai vowels and tone marks.

rules.name: The Flat Floor Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest are flat. Separate them with hairlines and tonal fills, not shadows. Only floating layers get a real shadow.

dos: **Do** use the existing classes in `src/styles/globals.css` (`panel`, `panel-head`, `primary-btn`, `secondary-btn`, `field`, `status-*`, `summary-card`) before creating new ones, and add new rules next to related ones, including their responsive rules.
**Do** keep one forest-green primary action per view.
**Do** pair every status colour with its label and dot; colour is never the only signal.
**Do** separate surfaces with 1px Hairline borders and `#f0f1f3` row dividers.
**Do** design every new screen at 600px and 820px as well as desktop.
donts: **Don't** change or replace the SIRISOFT green theme, or hard-code colours outside `:root`.
**Don't** use status colours (amber, brick, teal) for decoration.
**Don't** add heavy shadows to cards at rest; only modals, dialogs and toasts float.
**Don't** build new modal backdrops; use the shared `Modal` and `ConfirmDialog`.
**Don't** put a bordered, tinted box inside a panel (a card in a card). Separate a summary row inside a panel with a 1px divider instead.
**Don't** add coloured stripes along a card edge; use the icon tile or a dot.
